title: HaloEdge / Redwood - Channel + GPU SaaS Integration Intro
summary: Introductory channel-partner discovery. Discussed HaloEdge go-to-market, integration patterns for onramp/reseller, GPU capacity provisioning, routing and billing models. Security (SOC2/SSO/KMS), pilot scope, and next steps for a small pilot and technical deep dive were agreed.
topics: deployment models (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
next_steps: Redwood to share partner integration one-pager and pricing matrix by 2028-06-04
HaloEdge to provide current GPU fleet inventory and preferred regions by 2028-06-06
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) week of 2028-06-11
Set up trial account and pilot model list (small batch) -- target start 2028-06-18
action_items: Erin Mills - Share partner integration one-pager + pricing spreadsheet - 2028-06-04
Marta Silva - Send list of internal stakeholders and current infra (K8s + regions) - 2028-06-06
Samir Patel - Prepare pilot runbook and minimal benchmark test plan - 2028-06-10

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Erin M (Redwood AE), Samir P (Redwood SE), Nora L (Redwood SE), Lena O (HaloEdge Partnerships), Derek W (HaloEdge CTO), Marta S (HaloEdge PM), Omar K (HaloEdge Infra)

[00:00] Erin Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Erin, I'm an AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Quick round robin?
[00:06] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, Lena here, head of partnerships at HaloEdge. Excited to chat about how we might resell or onramp Redwood to our customers.
[00:12] Derek Wu: Derek, CTO, I'll focus on infra and technical questions.
[00:15] Marta Silva: Marta, platform PM, will own pilot coordination.
[00:18] Omar Kahn: Omar, infra, will dig into network/KMS stuff.
[00:22] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood, SE. I'll talk through integration patterns and perf questions. Nora Li is on in case we need deep-dive infra.

[02:05] Erin Mills: Cool. Quick agenda: understand HaloEdge GTM and customers, inventory of GPU capacity and regions, discuss integration models (reseller vs onramp vs white-label), security/compliance, and set next steps. Anything to add?
[02:20] Lena Ortiz: No, that captures it. We're particularly interested in the reseller model where we can bundle Redwood inference with our managed GPU offering.

[04:30] Samir Patel: High level, Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). In partner flows we often do a routing integration where HaloEdge can route requests to either Redwood Hosted or a dedicated pool you manage. There are a couple of patterns - do you have a preference?
[04:50] Derek Wu: For our enterprise customers, we need predictable throughput and data isolation. So Dedicated sounds attractive, but cost is a big factor. We run mixed workloads: bursty chat and steady embedding pipelines.

[06:10] Marta Silva: Also curious about quotas and billing. If we resell, can final billing be routed through HaloEdge or do we need separate Redwood accounts per customer?

[06:35] Erin Mills: We support channel-billing where partners can resell under an MSP arrangement; pricing can be adjusted for partners. There's also a routed integration where requests hit your control plane and we meter they same--sorry--we meter via partner account. We'll share the pricing matrix.

[08:00] Omar Kahn: Network questions: for Dedicated or Private, we need VPC peering and KMS/HSM integration. How mature are your VPC onboarding playbooks?
[08:18] Nora Li: We have a formal VPC onboarding doc, and for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM options. Some transcription note: sometimes our internal docs call it Redwood Private or R-Private, acronyms vary.

[10:05] Derek Wu: On performance: our customers want sub-60ms token latency for small chat messages on the front end. Can Redwood meet that on hosted instances? And how does routing to cheaper quantized models affect latency/cost?
[10:28] Samir Patel: For tail latency sub-60ms, that depends on model size and sequence length. For smaller models (7B quantized) you can often hit <60ms on dedicated A100 / H100-like hardware for 8k context, but for larger models you'll see higher latency. We do automatic fallback policies: if the primary model is overloaded, requests can be routed to a cheaper variant. There is a quality/cost tradeoff.

[12:00] Lena Ortiz: Are there known customers using a similar reseller pattern? Any case studies?
[12:10] Erin Mills: Yes, we've done partner onramps with two channel partners - one focused on regulated healthcare and one on financial services. We can share redacted references and a one-pager.

[13:30] Derek Wu: Regarding caching and batching - our batch embedding pipelines are throughput-sensitive; can Redwood support per-tenant batching or prefix caching?
[13:45] Samir Patel: Yes, we have workload-aware batching and prefix/KV cache. Note that KV cache behavior is sensitive with offloaded key-value caching -- sometimes in notes it's written K V cache which confuses people, apologies for the transcript noise. For embeddings we recommend batching strategies and provide suggestions via Redwood Optimize.

[15:20] Marta Silva: From the pilot perspective, we want a small set of customers (2-3) with varied workloads: realtime chat, embeddings for search, and a reranking job. What's the minimal pilot you recommend?
[15:36] Samir Patel: A minimal pilot would be: 1) one realtime chat flow on a 7B quantized model to validate latency and routing; 2) an embeddings job for search using 384-d or 768-d vectors; 3) a rerank test on a lightweight model. Keep it to ~4 weeks so we can iterate. We'll provide test prompts, eval harness, and success criteria.

[17:00] Lena Ortiz: That timeline works. On the legal side, procurement asked about data residency and retention -- they want logs to be retained only in EU for EU customers. How flexible is Redwood on per-tenant data residency?
[17:18] Erin Mills: We support per-region routing and can pin a customer to EU-hosted models and Dedicated capacity. For hosted API, we have region endpoints. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll share our data residency options.

[19:10] Omar Kahn: SOC2 and ISO certifications? Our security team will need copies of SOC2 and any pen-test reports. Also SSO: we use SAML and OIDC for dashboard access.
[19:25] Nora Li: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant and we have an ISO attestation in process. We support SAML, OIDC and SCIM for user provisioning. We can share SOC2 and the security questionnaire.

[21:00] Derek Wu: How do on-prem/private deployments work for air-gapped setups? Some of our financial customers need air-gapped inference.
[21:13] Samir Patel: We have an on-prem package that ships with a private control plane; note that some kernel/driver versions are sensitive and we maintain an ops guide. It's more involved but supported. For air-gapped, we also offer a turn-key appliance option with limited cloud-connected telemetry.

[23:40] Marta Silva: Ok cost question: partners are concerned about unit economics. If we route through a dedicated pool with autoscaling, how predictable are the costs for a reseller?
[23:58] Erin Mills: Dedicated pools are billed as reserved capacity plus any burst; we provide cost reports and token-level breakdowns in the Redwood Console so you can map costs to customers. For resellers we can set up metering so HaloEdge sees tenant-level usage. There's a chunk on cost controls: batching, quantization, and model selection are levers.

[26:10] Lena Ortiz: On the integration side, what's the simplest technical pattern: 1) HaloEdge proxies calls through your hosted API and we bill customers, or 2) we set up our own dedicated pools and route from our control plane to the pools?
[26:30] Samir Patel: Both are valid. Proxying to Hosted is fastest for GTM. Using dedicated pools you manage gives you control and better SLAs. We can also do hybrid: start with a hosted routed flow (fast) then migrate heavy customers to dedicated instances.

[28:50] Derek Wu: We have a legacy billing system -- any sample integration docs for metering and billing export?
[29:00] Erin Mills: We'll include billing APIs and sample CSV exports. Also partners can request longer retention of usage logs as an add-on.

[31:15] Lena Ortiz: For marketing: co-branded joint customers - what assets do you provide?
[31:25] Erin Mills: We have co-marketing kits, solution briefs, and partner case study templates. We'll share the kit in the follow up.

[33:00] Marta Silva: Can we run a small perf benchmark before the pilot with our sample model? We want to validate latency in our regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast).
[33:12] Samir Patel: Yes. We can provision a temporary dedicated small cluster or run hosted benchmarks with pinned model variants. We'll need your model list and sample prompts. Expect the bench to take 3-5 days to schedule.

[35:40] Omar Kahn: Regarding security again, we need to know where logs live, whether audit logs are immutable, and retention policy.
[35:52] Nora Li: Audit logs can be exported to your S3/GCS and we support immutability options via object locks. Retention configurable. We'll add specific docs.

[38:00] (brief cross-talk)
[38:15] Derek Wu: One more thing - quantization. Our customers ask about 4-bit quantized models. What are the tradeoffs and are there verified performance numbers?
[38:30] Samir Patel: We support quantized model variants and Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization based on workload. Tradeoffs: lower accuracy on some tasks, but huge cost savings. We have internal perf profiles across GPU types; we'll share a short matrix. Note: sometimes our docs call it 4Q/8Q etc and that confuses people.

[41:05] Lena Ortiz: Good. Pilot success metrics? What do you usually use?
[41:12] Samir Patel: For partners we suggest: latency P95 under X ms for chat, embeddings throughput per GPU target, cost per 1M tokens, and error/quality regression thresholds measured via eval prompts. We'll provide an eval harness.

[44:00] (quiet, notes being taken)
[44:22] Erin Mills: Let's recap action items and next steps. Samir, can you outline the tech-deep-dive ask?
[44:30] Samir Patel: Sure. SE deep dive to include: 1) details on routing patterns and API proxies; 2) VPC peering and KMS integration steps; 3) pilot benchmark plan and scripts; 4) observability and billing export mechanics. We'll propose a 60–90 minute session with HaloEdge infra and platform.

[46:10] Lena Ortiz: Works for us. Who's leading legal/procurement on your side for the partner contract?
[46:18] Erin Mills: I'll connect you to our Partnerships legal lead, Claire Jensen, in the follow up. Expect an initial partner MSA and then an SOW for pilot.

[48:00] Marta Silva: Timeline check again: pricing and doc share by 6/4, we send fleet inventory by 6/6, SE deep dive week of 6/11, pilot start target 6/18.
[48:18] Erin Mills: Yep that's the plan.

[50:00] Derek Wu: A small nit — how do we maintain model versioning across migrations? If we start hosted and move to dedicated, can we pin model versions so customers don't see regressions?
[50:15] Samir Patel: Yes. Redwood supports model pinning and rollouts. We also have automatic fallback policies and quality monitoring with alerts tied to evals and prompt sets.

[52:30] Lena Ortiz: Any concerns from Redwood about HaloEdge routing or reseller abuse?
[52:40] Erin Mills: We do standard partner onboarding and require partners to adhere to acceptable use policies. We'll provision partner keys with rate limits and usage quotas.

[54:00] (short silence)
[54:12] Omar Kahn: On the technical deep dive, we'll want to bring our SRE and networking folks. Also permissioning: can we sync RBAC to our identity provider?
[54:25] Nora Li: We support SAML and SCIM for RBAC sync; we can map groups to roles. We'll include sample mappings.

[56:00] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. Anything else?
[56:05] Marta Silva: No, all good.
[56:12] Erin Mills: Great. We'll follow up with the materials and proposed SE session times. Thanks everyone.
[56:20] Derek Wu: Thanks.
[56:22] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all.

(End 16:02 UTC ~62 minutes after start)

Notes on transcript: minor transcription artifacts present (product names sometimes truncated, acronyms like K V cache as separate tokens). Some speaker labels were simplified in the export (e.g., Speaker 2 vs Derek in short spots).
